From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May 2 capacity playbook — pipeline signals to fleet

Hannah — looping you in for the weekly alignment. Acme expanded this week: they converted the pilot PO into a 6-month reserved workload and are asking for guidance on sizing dedicated capacity. Quick summary below: 

- Customer: Acme Industries (NLP summarization / retrieval workload)
- Expected steady throughput: ~250 concurrent sessions during peak (0900-1700 PST)
- Model target: Llama-3-70B-8bit or equivalent quantized variant
- Request: recommendation for dedicated GPU count + recommended autoscale headroom and rollout plan

Attached is the initial pipeline estimate I pulled from the commercial team (20270502_acme_pipeline_estimate.xlsx). Finance would like a ballpark of monthly committed spend vs. on-demand. Infrastructure needs the expected qps/seq-length distribution to map to instance types. 

Questions for this thread: 
1) Marcus / Vivek — can you propose an initial dedicated pool spec (GPU type, count, burst policy) that satisfies latency SLO of 150ms p95 for prompt+generation (avg seq len 512)?
2) Laura — can we run a quick TCO compare (reserved vs burst for 6 months) tied to the attached estimate?
3) Samir — can you confirm expected go-live window and any procurement constraints (billing entity, PO cadence)?

Action: If we can get initial numbers by EOD Wed (05/04) we can include them in the Finance review on Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270502_acme_pipeline_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>

Subject: Re: May 2 capacity playbook — pipeline signals to fleet

Thanks Karthik — confirmed on our side. A few clarifications from procurement / engineering at Acme: 

- Go-live target: pilot expand to production ramp starting 2027-05-16, steady state by 2027-06-01.
- Billing: monthly invoicing to Acme P.O. #475-2027; procurement prefers reserved commitment but needs cost delta for approvals.
- Expected traffic profile: morning spike (0900–1100) roughly 35% of daily volume; average seq len ~480, 99th percentile ~2k tokens for long queries.
- Compliance ask: SOC2 evidence and proof of isolation for dedicated pool — we will circulate a security questionnaire next week.

We appreciate a short recommendation and what the canary rollout would look like.

—Samir
Head of Product Operations
Acme Industries
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 May 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May 2 capacity playbook — pipeline signals to fleet

Vivek/Marcus — thanks for the heads up. Marcus & I ran a quick spike test using a quantized L3-70B variant on g5.48x with batch fusion; notes and recommended sizing below (summarized):

Observed (test conditions approximate):
- 1 x g5.48x (8x A100-equivalent) under continuous batching handled ~40 concurrent low-latency sessions at p95=~140ms for 512 tokens and beamless decoding.
- With long tails (~2k tokens) p95 climbed to ~420ms without KV cache optimization per user.

Initial recommendation (conservative, supports burst & canary):
- Dedicated pool: 4 x g5.48x nodes (expected steady concurrent capacity ~160 sessions)
- Autoscale headroom: configure burst layer to allow +2 nodes (soft cap) for short-term spikes; aggressive prefix KV caching enabled
- Canary plan: deploy 1 node of the dedicated pool as canary for 72 hours starting 2027-05-16; route 10% of traffic, monitor latency, costs, and failure rates
- Fallback: fallback routing to hosted-compatible variant (L3-70B-8bit lower memory profile) if latency > 300ms p95 for 15 minutes

Estimated monthly committed spend (approx): 4 x g5.48x reserved = ~USD 172k/mo (hardware + support uplift). Burst-on-demand for the +2 nodes estimated incremental cost: USD 24k/mo average (depending on hours). Laura — these are rough, please refine with pricing model.

Action items: 
- Marcus: prepare runbook for canary + fallback (include KV caching toggles and rollout playbook) — due Thu 05/05 EOD
- Laura: detailed cost comparison reserved vs. burst for 6 months (include break-even) — due Thu 05/05 12:00 PT
- Karthik: confirm sales acceptance criteria and procurement timeline; ensure deal terms reflect the reserved commitment and fallback SLAs

Please include any security notes — Samir, expect SOC2 artifacts next week.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Capacity Planning (Sales Ops liaison)
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: May 2 capacity playbook — pipeline signals to fleet

Short update — ran the pricing delta and a 6-month model. High-level conclusions: 

- Reserved 4 x g5.48x (6-month commitment) vs. on-demand mix yields ~21% cost savings over pure on-demand for baseline hours.
- If Acme expects the morning spike to be sustained (35% of daily) and long-tail traffic persists, adding the +2 node burst layer (on-demand) is cost-efficient versus buying 2 extra reserved nodes upfront.
- Break-even: Approximately 3.5 months assuming current forecast in the attachment.

I will upload the detailed workbook to the Drive link and flag the cells used for the break-even analysis. Next steps: finalize commitment language (billing cadence + SLA credits) — Karthik I can draft redlines if you want.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
